source_name: NBS – Metodické usmernenia, stanoviská a odporúčania
why_relevant: Soft-law layer (methodological guidance, opinions, recommendations) that often follows a consultation and carries de-facto compliance dates without being a formal measure. Frequently the concrete supervisory expectation a bank must implement.

Official push channel for NBS publications; the consultation pages offer no dedicated RSS, so email subscription is the sanctioned low-latency alerting mechanism for new consultation and measure notices.

source_name: MF SR – Finančný trh (financial market policy hub)
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance owner-page for banking & payment services, capital market, insurance, intermediation, consumer protection and international sanctions, each split into 'Legislatíva' and 'Európska agenda'. The European-agenda subsections are where transposition intentions and EU-file positions surface before national drafts.

source_name: MF SR / fininfo.sk – Bankovníctvo legislation section
why_relevant: MF SR's financial-information portal listing banking legislation in force and links to amendments; useful as a cross-check that a consulted draft has actually become law and on what date.

source_name: MF SR – Tlačové správy (press releases on draft measures)
why_relevant: MF SR announces intended banking measures here often before or alongside MPK (observed: 'Návrh opatrení na ochranu klientov bánk' — proposal to increase bank price transparency and client protection). Gives political framing and intended timing that the legal text omits.

source_name: NR SR – parliamentary bill tracking (Národná rada SR)
why_relevant: After MPK, the draft goes to parliament where the dôvodová správa (explanatory memorandum), committee amendments and the final effective date are decided — the stage where compliance deadlines most often shift. Document previews (DocID-addressed) carry the explanatory memoranda that state transposition deadlines explicitly.

source_name: Rokovania vlády SR – government meeting materials portal
why_relevant: The stage between MPK and parliament: government session agendas and the full submitted material, including the vyhodnotenie pripomienok (evaluation of comments) showing which industry objections were accepted. Accessible without login.
The Government Legislative Council reviews drafts post-MPK; its agendas reveal which financial-market bills are moving and when, a scheduling signal ahead of the government session.

source_name: LexAPI (Essential Data) – commercial legislative-monitoring REST API
why_relevant: Commercial REST API aggregating legislative processes from both Slov-Lex and NR SR with attribute filtering and change feeds. Solves the JS-rendering and polling problems of Slov-Lex; the pragmatic backbone for an automated deadline tracker if licensing is acceptable.

EPI (Poradca podnikateľa) mirrors and indexes Slov-Lex legislative processes with editorial summaries; useful as a second, more scrape-friendly view and to catch items whose titles are opaque on the primary portal.

Law-firm/legal-media digest of ongoing MPK items with commentary; a cheap human-curated filter that flags which consultations the SK legal market considers material, and often summarises deadlines in plain language.

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) – novinky a tlačové správy
why_relevant: The only association representing SK banks; it files hromadné pripomienky in MPK and publicises its positions. Reveals industry objections and the practical implementation burden of a draft — the counter-party view to the regulator's, and a leading indicator of which deadlines will slip.

Sub-view of the comment register showing collective/mass comments, which trigger mandatory rozporové konanie (dispute resolution meeting) and therefore predictably delay a measure. High-value early warning that a deadline will move.

source_name: MF SR – Finančné inovácie / regulatory sandbox consultation track
why_relevant: MF SR's Centrum finančných inovácií with NBS ran an explicit consultation paper on sandbox design to collect market feedback; this track is where fintech/payments-specific SK consultations appear outside the standard MPK channel.

English mirror of NBS legislation/decree pages (observed for Decree 8/2022). Useful for cross-lingual entity matching and for analysts without Slovak, but coverage of live consultations is thinner than the SK tree — treat SK as canonical.

source_name: SLOV-LEX e-Zbierka – consolidated texts of banking/payments acts
why_relevant: Consolidated, date-versioned texts of zákon č. 483/2001 Z. z. o bankách and zákon č. 492/2009 Z. z. o platobných službách, with per-version effective dates (e.g. payment services act versions effective 17.1.2025, 8.4.2025, and a change effective 1.5.2026). Lets a consultation be tied to the exact compliance date it produced.

source_name: zakonypreludi.sk / autora.sk – commercial consolidated-law mirrors with version timelines
why_relevant: Third-party mirrors of SK acts that expose clean version timelines and future effective dates (autora.sk surfaced the 1.5.2026 change to the Payment Services Act). Far easier to parse than the official portal; use as a discovery aid, always confirming against Slov-Lex.

Slovak vendor of payment solutions and banking information systems; its reference page names an unusually complete roster of SK banks as customers (365.bank, Tatra banka, UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, VUB, CSOB, Privatbanka), making it a direct signal of which private banks buy payment/reporting software and from whom.

Publishes named, narrative case studies of SK bank projects (CSOB digital onboarding / remote identity verification, Tatra banka face-biometrics onboarding, Slovenska sporitelna branch system across ~190 branches, Raiffeisen unified front end). Compliance-driven onboarding/KYC spend is exactly the signal this cell needs and is invisible in public procurement portals.

Historically Asseco Slovakia; core-banking and building-savings-bank software vendor for CE. Reference page plus banking solution pages indicate which SK financial institutions run its core banking system — the platform on which regulatory reporting changes must be implemented.

source_name: EEA – Referencie filtered to 'banky a finančný sektor'
why_relevant: Slovak software house with a reference listing that is explicitly filterable to the banking/finance segment — a pre-segmented, low-noise list of bank engagements. The query-string filter makes it a cheap recurring collection target.

source_name: Goldmann Systems – Digital finance case studies (365.bank transformation)
why_relevant: Vendor case study naming a named SK bank programme (transformation of digital 365.bank into a full-service bank). Full-service licensing implies regulatory, reporting and product-compliance workstreams — a direct compliance-spend signal for a private bank.

SK software vendor whose reference material covers digital transformation of banking processes (branch time reduction, sales process). Secondary but useful for mapping the mid-tier vendor bench serving SK banks.

Large SK integrator listing finance among its reference sectors; useful for infrastructure/DORA-adjacent resilience and ICT third-party spend at banks, which never appears in public portals for private banks.

Long-established SK IT infrastructure / security / ITSM provider; reference page is a route to bank ICT-security and operational-resilience engagements relevant to DORA and NBS supervisory expectations.
SK-headquartered security vendor publishing enterprise references; relevant for cyber/ICT-risk supplier relationships at financial institutions under DORA and NIS2 pressure.

Qualified electronic signature / trust-service provider publishing named financial-sector implementations (e.g. Tatra Leasing online client solutions). eIDAS-driven and directly tied to regulatory-compliance procurement by SK financial institutions.

source_name: TOUCHIT / BrandIT tlačový servis – banking vendor & bank press releases
why_relevant: SK tech press-release wire that carries verbatim bank and vendor announcements, including compliance-driven deployments (e.g. Tatra banka's digital client-data update driven by SK and EU obligations, using state-register lookups). Press-release wires surface vendor wins before they reach vendor case-study pages.

SK financial trade outlet that covers joint bank infrastructure programmes (e.g. the instant-payments programme run jointly by Tatra banka, VUB and Slovenska sporitelna) — multi-bank infrastructure moves imply shared vendor selection and deadline-driven spend.
